newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac to give rare TV interview on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to give rare TV interview on Thursday.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will give a rare live television interview on Thursday amid gloom over high unemployment, sluggish economic growth and fears of guerrilla bombs.

TF1 television said on Monday that the president, under pressure for weeks to speak out to reassert the direction of the embattled government, would be interviewed by a panel of five reporters for an hour from 8.50 p.m. (1950 GMT).
It will be his first such television appearance since July.
"He is due to defend continuing the same policies with the same prime minister," the daily Liberation said on Monday, saying Chirac's mission would be to reassure a gloomy nation.

Chirac has repeatedly stated his confidence in fellow-Gaullist Prime Minister Alain Juppe despite even though Juppe's popularity is at record lows. Juppe says he expects to lead the government into the next legislative elections in 1998.

The government has suffered setbacks ranging from a bomb on a Paris train by suspected Algerian Moslem militants last week that killed four people to sleaze probes into members of Chirac's ruling Gaullist party.
It has also faced calls from within its own coalition for a relaxation of budget rigour aimed at enabling France to qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
Chirac has given no hint he might soften policy in a bid to revive economic growth and cut near-record unemployment.
